title: Signature Missing-field queries — Absence-Based Search
description: Signature original — The simplest absence query lists records lacking a required field: 'WHERE author IS NULL'. Indexes need explicit null handling since missing values are not indexed like present ones. Missing-field queries drive data-quality dashboards. This record documents a Signature-authored original method of the JAH archive toolkit, clearly labeled as Signature work rather than a public record.
demo:
# Absence-based search: find records missing required fields or characteristics.
records = [{'id': 'r1', 'author': 'A', 'year': 2020}, {'id': 'r2', 'year': 2021}, {'id': 'r3', 'author': 'B'}]
required = ['author', 'year']
absent_terms = []
def missing_fields(rec):
    return [f for f in required if f not in rec or rec[f] in (None, "", [])]
print("Required fields:", required, "| must-not-contain:", absent_terms or "none")
for r in records:
    miss = missing_fields(r)
    text = " ".join(str(v) for v in r.values()).lower()
    bad = [t for t in absent_terms if t.lower() in text]
    if miss or bad:
        print(f"  {r['id']}: missing {miss or '-'}; unwanted terms {bad or '-'}")
provenance: Signature-authored original method created for the JAH archive toolkit; clearly labeled Signature, not a public record.
